PAPERS.title: Air Pollution Triggers Metabolomic Signature of Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Mice and Humans: Implications for Cardiovascular Disease Development.
PAPERS.pm: Diesel exhaust (ApoE-/- mice, 2 wk) and a natural LA-to-Beijing move (PM2.5 14.4 -> 67.6 ug/m3, 10 wk)
PAPERS.geo: USA and China (Los Angeles-Beijing travel panel)
PAPERS.n: A cross-species design: ApoE-/- mice given two weeks of diesel exhaust, and 26 healthy adults who moved from Los Angeles (PM2.5 14.4 ug/m3) to Beijing (67.6 ug/m3) for ten weeks. Multi-platform metabolomics and lipidomics converged on long-chain dicarboxylic acids and medium-to-long-chain acylcarnitines rising in both species, consistent with impaired fatty-acid oxidation; Seahorse respirometry confirmed hepatic mitochondrial dysfunction in the mice, and in humans the shifts tracked 12-/15-LOX lipid peroxidation products and PAH exposure biomarkers. Tryptophan, pyrimidine and lysine signatures did not replicate across species. n=26 with a city-level exposure contrast that also changes diet, time zone and stress - no personal monitoring is reported. Relevance: a 4.7-fold ambient contrast is exactly where calibrated personal sensors would sharpen the dose axis.

PAPERS.title: Heart Function Changes During Environmentally Relevant Combined Exposure to Heat, Ultrafine Carbon Black, and Ozone: Role of NOD-like Receptor X1.
PAPERS.pm: Ultrafine carbon black 2.5 mg/m3 + O3 1 ppm, with or without 36 C heat, 3 h
PAPERS.n: Female Nlrx1+/+ and Nlrx1-/- mice received 3 h of filtered air, heat (36 C), ultrafine carbon black plus ozone (2.5 mg/m3 + 1 ppm), or all three, with echocardiography, BAL and cardiac mitochondrial assays at 2 and 24 h. UfCB+O3 alone cut stroke volume, cardiac output and complex III-V activity in both genotypes; the triple exposure produced larger falls in ejection fraction and fractional shortening, more pulmonary neutrophilia and dyssynchronous strain in the knockouts, and heat alone impaired mitochondrial function only in Nlrx1-/-. Doses are two to three orders above ambient and the particle and ozone arms are never separated, so particle-specific attribution is not possible. Relevance: supports co-logging temperature with PM at every sensor node, since heat modifies the cardiac response.

PAPERS.title: Acute co-exposure to urban particulate matter and aircraft noise elicits lung-centered immune-redox proteomic remodeling in mice.
PAPERS.pm: NIST SRM 1648a urban PM, 3 days, alone and with aircraft noise
PAPERS.n: DIA LC-MS/MS proteomics of lung, brain and heart from male C57BL/6J mice given three days of NIST SRM 1648a urban PM, aircraft noise, both, or control - the exposure model previously characterised by Kuntic et al. The lung dominated: PM+noise gave the broadest induction of acute-phase, phagosome, interferon and macrophage proteins, with NADPH oxidase, iron handling, barrier and endothelial/ECM changes that agree with the parent study's NOX-2, HO-1, ROS, blood-pressure and vascular endpoints. Most stress proteins scaled proportionally rather than synergistically; brain and heart responses were smaller. Dose is a standard reference material, not a measured airborne concentration in the abstract, and only males were used. Relevance: noise and PM co-vary along the same roads, so co-located acoustic and PM sensing is the matching exposure design.

PAPERS.title: APOE genotype shapes persistent behavioral and molecular alterations following early postnatal particulate matter exposure in humanized apoE3 and apoE4 mice.
PAPERS.pm: NIST SRM 2787 fine PM, whole-body inhalation 1 h/day PND4-14, nominal max 3789 ug/m3 (not measured)
PAPERS.n: Humanized apoE3 and apoE4 mice of both sexes inhaled NIST fine PM (SRM 2787) or saline for 1 h/day across postnatal days 4-14, then underwent behavioural testing to PND96 and hippocampal/striatal expression profiling. Genotype, not PM, was the main determinant: apoE4 animals were more anxiety-like with hippocampal reorganisation of synaptic, glutamatergic, glial and redox pathways. PM produced only subtle social-behaviour effects and suggestive sex- and region-dependent marker changes. The authors state the chamber concentration was a nominal theoretical maximum of 3789 ug/m3 and was never measured - an unquantified dose, which makes the null-leaning PM result uninterpretable in dose-response terms. Relevance: a clean example of why exposure chambers need the same real-time mass verification as field sensors.

PAPERS.title: Effects of Traffic-Related Diesel Exhaust Exposure and Moderate Exercise on Obesity, Metabolic Dysfunction, and Inflammatory Responses in Rats.
PAPERS.pm: Diesel exhaust, mean 300 ug/m3 PM2.5, 2 or 4 h/day for 8 weeks
PAPERS.n: 48 female Wistar rats randomised to six groups: diesel exhaust at a mean 300 ug/m3 PM2.5 for 2 or 4 h/day over eight weeks, with or without 30 min/day moderate treadmill exercise. Exhaust raised body weight, BMI, Lee index, visceral adiposity index, LDL, triglycerides, glucose, leptin, CRP, IL-1b, IL-6 and TNF-a and lowered HDL and insulin (all p<0.001), most strongly at 4 h/day; exercise attenuated but did not abolish these changes. Only p-values are reported - no effect sizes - and whole exhaust cannot separate particles from NO2 and CO. 300 ug/m3 is a high-traffic peak, not a typical mean. Relevance: the exposure-by-activity interaction argues for pairing wearable PM with accelerometry, since ventilation rate rises with exercise.

PAPERS.title: Atmospheric Particulate Matter as a Carrier of Pb, Cd, and Ni: From Environmental Transfer and Bioaccessibility to Molecular Toxicity and Predictive Modeling.
PAPERS.pm: PM-bound Pb, Cd and Ni across the source-to-effect continuum
PAPERS.n: A narrative review tracing PM-bound lead, cadmium and nickel from emission through transport, deposition, food-chain transfer, bioaccessibility and toxicokinetics to molecular toxicity and predictive modelling. The central argument is that total PM mass and total metal concentration misrepresent biologically effective dose, which also depends on respiratory deposition, dissolution kinetics, gastrointestinal release and co-associated constituents; the three metals share oxidative, inflammatory, mitochondrial, genomic and epigenetic effects but differ in mobility and target organs. No search strategy or quality appraisal is described, so coverage cannot be judged, and no quantitative synthesis is offered. Relevance: a reminder that optical mass sensing is blind to exactly the metal fraction that drives toxicity; composition needs periodic filter sampling alongside.

PAPERS.title: Long-term exposure to fine particulate matter constituents and incident stroke risk among middle-aged and older adults in China: a cohort study.
PAPERS.pm: TAP-dataset PM2.5 and five constituents (SO4, NO3, NH4, OM, BC) at residence
PAPERS.n: CHARLS 2013-2018: 8,724 adults, 610 incident strokes over a median 5.0 years, with PM2.5 and five constituents from the TAP reanalysis. Per IQR, HRs were 1.55 (95% CI 1.35-1.79) for PM2.5, 1.55 for sulfate, 1.37 for nitrate, 1.42 for ammonium, 1.59 for organic matter and 1.77 (1.54-2.03) for black carbon; quantile g-computation gave BC the largest mixture weight (28.6%). Susceptibility was higher above 65 and in southern China. Stroke is self-reported physician diagnosis, constituents are strongly collinear model outputs, and IQRs differ by constituent, so per-IQR HRs are not directly comparable. Still the clearest signal this week that carbonaceous particles carry the cerebrovascular risk. Relevance: argues for adding absorption (BC) channels to low-cost nodes, not just scattering mass.

PAPERS.title: When air gets heavy: joint PM(2.5) and ambient humidity exposure, frailty, and stroke.
PAPERS.pm: Annual PM2.5 and relative humidity at residence, dichotomised at median
PAPERS.n: CHARLS (n=17,197) plus a single-centre hospital sample (n=782), with annual PM2.5 and relative humidity dichotomised at database medians. High PM2.5 gave HR 1.184 (95% CI 1.083-1.295) for incident stroke in CHARLS and OR 1.846 (1.247-2.733) in the hospital sample; high humidity HR 1.112; joint high-high exposure HR 1.361 (1.171-1.582). Frailty mediated 18.1% of the PM2.5 association. Median dichotomisation discards the exposure-response shape, the hospital arm is cross-sectional, and humidity at annual resolution is largely a climate-zone proxy confounded with region. Relevance: humidity is also the dominant bias term in optical PM sensors - an epidemiologic humidity effect estimated from sensor-derived PM would be partly an artefact, so correction must precede the health model.

PAPERS.title: Mitochondrial DNA methylation as a bridge: Linking indoor air purification to alleviated cardiovascular impairments in young adults.
PAPERS.pm: Personal PM2.5 under true vs sham indoor air purification (47.45% indoor reduction)
PAPERS.n: A randomised double-blind crossover of true versus sham air purification in 38 healthy young adults. Purification cut indoor PM2.5 by 47.45%. Each 10 ug/m3 rise in personal PM2.5 at lag 24-48 h was associated with mtATP6 hypomethylation, and mtDNA hypomethylation mediated 14.87% (p=0.04) of the PM2.5 association with D-dimer at lag 0 h, among 16 cardiovascular indicators tested. The mediation analyses run across many CpG sites, lags and outcomes with no stated multiplicity correction, and the headline p=0.04 would not survive one. Short crossover periods in young adults cannot show clinical benefit. Relevance: personal PM2.5 was the analysed exposure, so the intervention's value rests on personal-monitor accuracy - the device and its calibration are not reported in the abstract.

PAPERS.title: Association of preconception to early childhood residential greenness with child neurodevelopmental outcomes and the mediating role of air pollution: a prospective cohort study.
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5, PM10, NO2, O3 as single-pollutant mediators of NDVI
PAPERS.n: 5,284 mother-child pairs in the Jiangsu Birth Cohort, with satellite NDVI from preconception to early childhood and Bayley-III screening at age three. Per 0.1 NDVI, preconception and third-trimester greenness lowered risk of the emerging/at-risk cognition category (RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.74-0.98; 0.82, 0.71-0.95) and gross motor (0.87, 0.77-0.98; 0.77, 0.68-0.88), surviving FDR at 0.10. Single-pollutant mediation assigned 68.0% (PM10) and 63.5% (NO2) of the preconception-cognition association, and 59.1% via PM2.5 for third-trimester gross motor. Separate single-pollutant mediators summing well past 100% show the pollutants are proxies for one another and for urbanicity; mediation of that size in a greenness model needs sequential or joint mediation to be credible. Relevance: greenness-PM trade-offs are measurable only with sub-kilometre PM surfaces.

PAPERS.title: Investigating effects of day-to-day variations in environmental exposure on the human brain: study protocol for the Day2Day Environment project.
PAPERS.pm: Wearable air-quality, noise and light sensors with GPS tracking over 25 sessions
PAPERS.n: Protocol and dataset description for a dense longitudinal study: 30 participants, 25 testing sessions each, with wearable devices, GPS-based geospatial tracking and geographic ecological momentary assessment capturing air quality, noise, light, activity, stress, cognition and affect, paired with repeated MRI (T1/T2*, quantitative multi-parameter mapping, hippocampal proton density, DTI). No results. The abstract does not name the air-quality sensor, its calibration or which pollutants are logged, which is the component this watch would need to judge. n=30 is small but the within-person repeated design is where short-term neuroplasticity signals are detectable. Relevance: one of few designs coupling personal low-cost PM tracks to imaging; worth following when the sensor methods paper appears.

PAPERS.title: Impact of particulate matter 2.5 exposure on severity of pediatric chronic rhinitis: A prospective cohort study.
PAPERS.pm: 1-week mean ambient PM2.5 by inverse-distance weighting of monitors
PAPERS.n: 146 children with chronic rhinitis in the Bangkok Metropolitan Region followed weekly for a median 52 weeks (Jul 2024-Aug 2025), with symptom severity on a visual analogue scale and the preceding week's PM2.5 interpolated by inverse-distance weighting. Per 10 ug/m3, VAS rose by 0.260 (95% CI 0.215-0.306); the association held in both allergic and non-allergic rhinitis, with wet season, infections and medication also associated. The effect is small on a 10-point scale, the VAS is self- or parent-reported and unblinded to haze days, and IDW over sparse monitors ignores indoor exposure. Relevance: repeated weekly outcomes over a year are an ideal fit for home or school low-cost sensors, which would replace IDW with measured exposure.

PAPERS.title: Association between ambient PM(2.5) exposure during pregnancy and risk of preterm birth: a retrospective birth cohort study in Chengdu, Southwest China.
PAPERS.pm: Satellite-derived vs monitor-based PM2.5 across gestational windows
PAPERS.n: 35,136 singleton births at one Chengdu hospital, 2015-2024; 2,622 (7.46%) preterm. Mean whole-pregnancy PM2.5 was 49.1 ug/m3 (satellite) and 51.9 ug/m3 (monitors). Per 10 ug/m3, whole-pregnancy ORs were 1.089 (95% CI 1.010-1.174) satellite and 1.091 (0.996-1.195) monitor, with first- and third-trimester signals and landmark ORs 1.06-1.10 for weeks 32-35; associations were confined to late, not earlier, preterm birth. Single-hospital sampling, district-level fixed effects and residence at delivery limit the exposure contrast. The methodological result is the useful one: the two exposure products gave near-identical point estimates, with satellite giving complete coverage and narrower intervals. Relevance: a direct, if coarse, benchmark for when a sparse monitor network is adequate - the question dense sensor networks exist to answer at finer scale.

PAPERS.title: Spatio-temporal assessment of PM2.5 and PM10 pollution in core and peripheral municipalities of the Kathmandu valley using regulatory and low-cost sensor data
PAPERS.pm: Regulatory monitors integrated with a high-resolution low-cost sensor network, daily PM2.5/PM10, 2023-2024
PAPERS.n: Preprint integrating regulatory monitors with a dense low-cost sensor network across core and peripheral municipalities of the Kathmandu Valley, 2023-2024. Annual mean PM2.5 was 40.71 ug/m3 in the urban core versus 27.22 ug/m3 in the periphery; the core exceeded WHO guidelines on nearly all winter and pre-monsoon days, with a core amplification factor up to 1.60 in the dry season, contrasting size dominance, and evidence of long-range transport during extreme events. The abstract gives no sensor model, no calibration or co-location statistics and no sensor count, so the core-periphery gradient cannot yet be separated from sensor bias - critical in a valley with strong humidity and dust seasonality. Not peer reviewed. Relevance: exactly the hybrid-network use case, in a data-poor basin; the calibration section decides whether it is evidence.

PAPERS.title: Characterizing Ambient Fine Particulate Matter Pollution in Jordan: National Monitoring Evidence of Spatial Inequality, PM2.5 Hotspots, and Temporal Trends (2018-2024)
PAPERS.pm: Annual PM2.5 from Jordan's national monitoring network, 2018-2024
PAPERS.n: Preprint analysing annual PM2.5 across Jordan's national monitoring network, 2018-2024, by site class. Industrial-related sites averaged 26.51 ug/m3 versus 29.24 ug/m3 at urban-related sites (Mann-Whitney U=297, p=0.604), and the Sen's slope was -1.67 ug/m3/yr with significant governorate-level differences. The authors themselves flag that the network expanded over the period, so the declining trend is confounded by a changing site mix - a fixed-site subset analysis is the obvious missing check. Annual means only; no instrument type or completeness criteria are stated. Not peer reviewed. Relevance: a network-expansion artefact masquerading as a trend is the same failure mode that growing low-cost networks face.

PAPERS.title: Inter-annual trends of PM2.5-bound heavy metals in Dhaka, Bangladesh: a comparative study for source apportionment and health risk assessment
PAPERS.pm: Elevated-altitude PM2.5 filter sampling, heavy metals, PMF
PAPERS.n: Only the graphical-abstract summary was deposited: elevated-altitude PM2.5 sampling in Dhaka found PM2.5-bound heavy metals far above global guidelines, positive matrix factorisation resolved six emission sources, and Cr, Pb, Cd and Mn drove both non-cancer and cancer risk across all age groups. No concentrations, years, sample counts or factor identities are available from the deposit, so the inter-annual trend in the title cannot be evaluated, and deterministic risk quotients from filter metals typically assume total-metal bioavailability. Elevated-altitude sampling also under-represents street-level exposure. Relevance: Dhaka is a high-priority low-cost network setting where mass sensing needs exactly this kind of periodic compositional anchoring. Admitted on the summary; re-check when the full abstract resolves.

PAPERS.title: Can Electric Vehicles Reduce Summertime Air Pollution Exposure Inequalities in Metro Atlanta? A High-Resolution Analysis
PAPERS.pm: CMAQ at 1 km vs 12 km, NO2, MDA8 O3 and PM2.5 under 30% EV adoption
PAPERS.n: 1-km CMAQ simulations of 30% light- and heavy-duty EV adoption in metro Atlanta for summer. Domain-wide means fell 0.22 ppb NO2, 0.94 ppb MDA8 O3 and 0.06 ug/m3 PM2.5, with local NO2 and PM2.5 increases near power plants; the largest reductions fell in communities with higher Asian, Hispanic and Black shares, though disparities persisted. The PM2.5 change is well inside CMAQ's typical error and a single season. The most transferable result is methodological: 12-km runs underestimated minority exposure by up to 25% for NO2 and 10% for PM2.5 relative to 1 km. Relevance: that resolution bias is a quantitative argument for dense sensor networks in environmental-justice assessment, where coarse grids systematically understate the disparity.

PAPERS.title: 10-year trends of particle size distributions and equivalent black carbon at the Environmental-Climate Observatory (ECO) in Lecce (Italy).
PAPERS.pm: Online PM2.5, PM10-2.5, PNSD 10-10,000 nm, eBC; offline OC/EC for MAC, 2015-2024
PAPERS.n: A decade (2015-2024) of co-located online PM2.5, coarse PM, particle number size distribution (10-10,000 nm) and equivalent BC at a southern-Italian observatory, with offline OC/EC to derive the mass absorption cross-section. PM2.5 fell -2.58%/yr, eBC -3.17%/yr and total PNC -2.99%/yr (Aitken and accumulation modes), while PM10-2.5 was flat, held up by Saharan dust on 13.2% of days. MAC was stable at 12.4 +/- 2.4 m2/g, so falling absorption reflects falling eBC rather than changing optics; new particle formation occurred on about 25% of days. Single site, and the abstract gives neither the trend estimator nor uncertainty on the slopes. Relevance: a stable decade-long MAC is a rare field-validated constant for converting absorption to BC mass - and the fine/coarse decoupling under dust is precisely where low-cost optical sensors misreport.

PAPERS.title: Spatiotemporal Prediction of Sandstorm Utilizing Multi-Source Data and ConvLSTM Model: A Case Study in Northwest China
PAPERS.pm: Surface PM10 with Himawari-8/9 AOD assimilated by EnKF into ConvLSTM
PAPERS.n: Dust forecasting for photovoltaic operations in Gansu: surface PM10 and Himawari-8/9 AOD are assimilated with an ensemble Kalman filter and fed to a multi-scale ConvLSTM with a high-value-focused loss. At 4 h lead the model reached RMSE 30.1 ug/m3 and MAE 16.1 ug/m3, captured the evolution of an April 2024 regional event, and ran in under 30 s per simulation. Validation rests on one event, errors are not stratified by concentration (where dust peaks run to thousands of ug/m3), and no persistence baseline is reported, so skill over naive forecasting is unknown. Relevance: EnKF assimilation of surface PM is the natural entry point for low-cost sensor data into nowcasts - provided the sensors' known coarse-mode undercount under dust is corrected first.

PAPERS.title: Humidity-dependent photoacoustic absorption biases and effective water mass accommodation coefficients for multicomponent aerosol particles
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only - photoacoustic absorption bias vs RH, multicomponent aerosol

PAPERS.title: Comparative analysis of metal concentrations in respirable particles and nanoparticulate matter (NPM) from mild steel, aluminum, and stainless steel welding fumes.
PAPERS.pm: Breathing-zone respirable and NRD nanoparticle samplers; Mn, Fe, Cr, Ni, Cu, Al by ICP-OES
PAPERS.n: Breathing-zone respirable and nanoparticle respiratory deposition (NRD) samplers on 61 participants - 38 welders, 12 factory and 11 office controls - with ICP-OES metals and TEM/EDS morphology. Mild-steel fumes (n=31) were dominated by Mn and Fe, stainless (n=3) by Cr and Ni, aluminium (n=4) by Al; across the six metals, the nanoparticulate fraction carried 48.3% of the respirable metal mass on average, with substantial Mn, Cr and Ni in NPM. The stainless and aluminium arms are too small for inference, which the authors acknowledge. Relevance: if half the respirable metal sits below ~300 nm, optical sensors - which lose efficiency below that size - will systematically undercount the toxicologically dominant fraction in welding environments.

PAPERS.title: Assessing home environmental hazards for older adults receiving in-home supportive services: the healthy homes assessment tool.
PAPERS.pm: Consumer-grade indoor PM2.5 and radon monitors vs care-coordinator hazard ratings
PAPERS.n: Development and pilot validation of the Healthy Home Assessment Tool, a care-coordinator checklist for indoor air quality and moisture/mould embedded in home- and community-based services, in 41 low-income older-adult households (median age 76). Against consumer-grade IAQ monitors, 61.0% of homes exceeded 9 ug/m3 PM2.5 and 21.9% exceeded the 4 pCi/L radon action level; PM2.5 was higher where smoking was reported and fungal burden higher with visible mould. The comparison of indoor snapshots with an annual ambient standard overstates exceedance, and the consumer monitors are uncalibrated in the abstract. Relevance: a concrete pathway for low-cost PM sensors into social-care workflows - but the 61% figure depends entirely on a sensor whose bias is not stated.

PAPERS.title: Potential Link Between Indoor Air Quality and Coronary Artery Disease in Amsterdam, a Field Study
PAPERS.pm: Multi-week in-home PM2.5, PM10 and CO2 monitoring
PAPERS.n: Preprint: several weeks of in-home PM2.5, PM10 and CO2 monitoring in 49 patients referred for coronary CT angiography in two socioeconomically contrasting Amsterdam neighbourhoods (Zuid n=24, Nieuw-West n=25), compared with CAD-RADS, calcium scores, vessel involvement and obstructive disease. No systematic neighbourhood difference in indoor air was found, but within-neighbourhood variability was large, and indoor PM showed no significant association with CAD or obstructive CAD. A weeks-long snapshot cannot represent the decades of exposure behind coronary atherosclerosis, and n=49 is badly underpowered for a null. Not peer reviewed. Relevance: the within-neighbourhood spread is the durable finding - household factors dominate indoor PM, which area-level outdoor sensing cannot capture.

PAPERS.title: Energy-Indoor Air Quality-Health Nexus in Rural Residential Retrofits: A Field-Calibrated Coupled Simulation and Multi-Criteria Evaluation for the Central Plains Transitional Climate of China
PAPERS.design: Repeated field measurement with CFD simulation
PAPERS.pm: 72-h paired before/after indoor PM2.5, PM10, CO2, HCHO, TVOC; EnergyPlus-CONTAM co-simulation
PAPERS.n: Solid-fuel brick-concrete rural homes in Anyang, Henan: 72-h paired winter and summer measurements of PM2.5, PM10, CO2, formaldehyde and TVOC calibrate a two-way EnergyPlus-CONTAM model (indoor temperature NMBE -2.1%, CV(RMSE) 6.7%). An envelope-only retrofit cut thermal loads 52.2% but raised winter PM2.5 25.8% and formaldehyde 32.4% via a 62.3% fall in infiltration; adding schedule-optimised natural ventilation kept 95.6% of savings while cutting the PM2.5 hazard quotient 20.3%. Calibration and out-of-sample validation are reported for temperature and CO2, not for PM, so the PM results rest on unvalidated source and deposition terms; single author, one county. Relevance: tightening envelopes raises indoor PM from solid fuel - retrofit programmes need indoor sensors to catch it.

PAPERS.title: Impacts of Housing Retrofits on Indoor Environmental Quality and Energy Consumption: A Review
PAPERS.pm: Indoor PM2.5, VOCs, NO2, HCHO, radon, CO2, T and RH before and after retrofit
PAPERS.n: A review of residential retrofit studies. Retrofits cut energy use by 10-84%; indoor temperature rises for winter-targeted and falls for summer-targeted measures, but effects on RH, CO2 and pollutants including PM2.5 varied with ventilation, occupant behaviour and outdoor levels. The authors' main conclusion is critical of the evidence base: most studies lacked a causal framework, long observation, adequate samples, weather adjustment, matched controls and behaviour control. No pooled estimate and no search protocol in the abstract. Read together with the Anyang simulation in this issue, the gap is clear. Relevance: long-duration, matched-control indoor PM monitoring with low-cost sensors is the cheapest way to supply the causal designs this review says are missing.

PAPERS.title: Spatial analysis of the burden of lung cancer attributable to long-term PM(2.5) exposure in Morocco: a national assessment using the WHO AirQ+ model.
PAPERS.pm: City-specific annual PM2.5 (2019) for 46 areas into WHO AirQ+
PAPERS.n: WHO AirQ+ applied to 2019 city-specific PM2.5 for 46 Moroccan urban and rural areas. PM2.5 ranged from 7.1 ug/m3 in coastal El Jadida (RR 1.02; attributable proportion 2.35%) to 28.4 ug/m3 in Errachidia (RR 1.30, 95% CI 1.17-1.42; AP 23.29%); Casablanca's moderate RR of 1.06 still yielded 24 attributable cases. The RRs are the model's concentration-response function evaluated at each city's mean, not observed associations, and a single year of concentration data - sources not specified, and Morocco's monitoring is sparse - drives everything. Southern desert areas likely carry a dust-dominated PM2.5 whose lung-cancer potency differs from the combustion-derived PM behind the CRF. Relevance: the uncertainty sits almost entirely in the exposure input, where a sensor network would change the answer most.

PAPERS.title: Air Pollution, Temperature, and Demographic Vulnerability as Determinants of Cause-Specific Mortality in Portugal.
PAPERS.pm: Monthly NO2 and PM2.5 exceedance above WHO 2021 guideline values
PAPERS.n: Nationwide monthly data for Portugal, 2010-2022, with GEE models of malignant, circulatory and respiratory mortality against NO2, PM2.5 and temperature, exposures coded as concentration above WHO 2021 guideline values. The signal is NO2, not PM: respiratory mortality RR 1.014 (95% CI 1.009-1.019) per 1 ug/m3 NO2 above guideline, circulatory 1.005; PM2.5 appears mainly as a modifier attenuating the NO2 association with tumour mortality, and pollutant findings were not robust in sensitivity analyses. A reported RR of 142.6 for males 65+ is a predicted risk ratio against a reference group, not an exposure effect. Monthly national aggregation is ecological and thresholding at guidelines discards most variance. Relevance: minimal; logged for the PM2.5-modifies-NO2 finding, which would need personal-scale data to test.

PAPERS.title: Implementing Community-Centered Air Quality Law: Success Stories From California's Assembly Bill 617.
PAPERS.pm: Community emissions reduction programme strategies across nine AB 617 communities
PAPERS.n: Mixed-methods comparison of community emissions reduction programmes (CERPs) in nine California AB 617 communities: over 800 strategies coded into 25 groups and rated on capacity for health protection, adoption pathway and ease of implementation, with funding expenditure as the progress proxy. Success tracked creative programme development, interagency coordination and community capacity. Expenditure is a process measure, not an air-quality or health outcome, and 'success stories' framing invites selection. Relevance: AB 617 is the largest statutory deployment of community air monitoring in the US, yet the abstract evaluates strategies without any measured concentration change - the monitoring data that could close that loop exist and are not used here.

PAPERS.title: Associations of temperature, particulate matter, and greenness with human papillomavirus positivity at screening: an analysis of Guangdong Province (2016-2022) using the treed distributed lag nonlinear model.
PAPERS.pm: Biweekly mean PM2.5 at examination date, treed DLNM over 24 weeks
PAPERS.n: Screening records for 1,287,412 women in Guangdong, 2016-2022, analysed with treed distributed-lag nonlinear models against biweekly temperature, PM2.5 and NDVI. High PM2.5 (97.5th percentile, 38.0 ug/m3 vs median 20.3) was associated with higher odds of HPV positivity over lag weeks 1-16 (cumulative OR 1.172, 95% CrI 1.051-1.283); low temperature and low NDVI also carried associations. The authors report that temporal sensitivity analyses attenuated the PM2.5 association. HPV positivity reflects acquisition months to years earlier and screening attendance is seasonal, so a weeks-scale lag structure is biologically implausible and likely confounded by attendance timing. Relevance: low; included as a caution on DLNM results with outcomes whose latency does not match the lag window.
